title: Time zones were invented for trains
summary: Before railways, every town kept its own solar time. Train timetables forced countries — Sweden included — to adopt shared standard time in the 1800s.

scenes.text: Time zones were invented for trains.
Towns once set clocks by the sun. Local noon in Gothenburg came about 24 minutes after Stockholm's.
Fast railways turned that into chaos. Timetables needed one shared time.

events.what: British railways move to London time
US and Canadian railroads adopt time zones

scenes.text: In the US, railroads — not the government — set the zones.
scenes.reveal: Congress didn't make time zones law until 1918.

scenes.text: Technology doesn't just save time. Sometimes it defines it.
